cards.title: One Researcher Taped Out a RISC-V Chip in Five Weeks Using AI Agents and Formal Verification
cards.why_it_matters: This is a landmark demonstration of AI-directed autonomous hardware design at scale — the 'Salt method' of proof-kernel-gated agent coordination is a concrete, reproducible workflow that research engineers should study.
cards.summary: Using consumer AI subscriptions over five weeks, one researcher directed AI agents from application code through a verified compiler and executive to a RISC-V processor taped out on a community silicon shuttle. No RTL was written by a human; no proofs passed human review. The 'Salt method' routes all mathematical claims through a Lean 4 proof kernel and SAT-checked silicon equivalence, with a published error ledger reaching catch #256 and zero incorrect proofs reaching the record.

cards.title: VIALS Benchmark Exposes Frontier VLMs' Failures on Life-Sciences Visual Artifacts
cards.why_it_matters: As AI agents are increasingly deployed in scientific workflows, this benchmark directly quantifies a capability gap — frontier vision-language models fail on domain-specific scientific image interpretation that domain-expert humans find straightforward.
cards.summary: VIALS is a 161-task visual question-answering benchmark covering gel blots, microscopy images, plasmid maps, flow cytometry plots, and molecular structures drawn from real biotech workflows (not polished publication figures). Frontier vision-language models fail to accurately interpret these images despite fluency on natural images, revealing gaps in domain knowledge and domain-specific visual reasoning.

cards.title: PerturbRx Learns Drug-Induced Molecular Transitions to Predict Patient Cancer Treatment Response
cards.why_it_matters: Combining perturbation biology with representation learning for clinical drug-response prediction is a technically interesting approach relevant to researchers working on RL-style transition models or scientific ML for biomedicine.
cards.summary: PerturbRx trains a drug- and dose-conditioned latent transition predictor on context-matched but cell-unpaired control and treated single-cell populations, then transfers frozen predictors to pretreatment patient profiles — no post-treatment measurements needed. Combining predicted transitions with patient and drug representations, PerturbRx achieves the strongest aggregate predictive performance across TCGA and patient-derived xenograft benchmarks among evaluated methods.

cards.title: Squeezed Light Could Boost Detection of QED Vacuum Nonlinearity
cards.why_it_matters: Quantum ML and physics-informed AI researchers tracking experimental quantum foundations will want to know that photonic state engineering (including squeezed states) can meaningfully improve detectability of a fundamental QED prediction.
cards.summary: QED predicts vacuum behaves as a nonlinear medium. Experiments searching for this effect look for photons appearing in modes that would be empty without vacuum nonlinearity. Replacing the initial vacuum in that mode with classical or non-classical (e.g., squeezed) photon states is shown to significantly improve detectability of the signal.

cards.title: New Accelerated Newton Method Hits O(1/k³) Without Cubic Regularization Subproblems
cards.why_it_matters: Optimization methods underpin virtually all ML training; a second-order method achieving O(1/k³) convergence with only one linear solve per iteration and no nonlinear subproblems is a meaningful algorithmic advance worth tracking.
cards.summary: A direct accelerated Newton method for convex functions with Lipschitz-continuous Hessian achieves O(1/k³) global convergence using only primal variables and one linear solve per iteration — no cubic regularization, nonlinear parameter search, or dual extragradient corrections required. Supports Hessian-free inexact solvers, Bregman divergence generalization, and composite optimization extensions.

cards.title: Exact Truthfulness Is Incompatible with Complete and Sound Calibration Measures
cards.why_it_matters: Calibration and truthfulness of probabilistic predictions are core concerns in ML evaluation and alignment; this impossibility result and the accompanying approximate-truthfulness constructions are theoretically significant for researchers in forecasting and online learning.
cards.summary: For sequential binary prediction, exact truthfulness in a calibration measure is proved incompatible with both completeness and soundness, even for independent outcomes. Two general reductions from a base measure yield additively and multiplicatively approximately truthful calibration measures. The multiplicative reduction produces a sound and complete measure that is (1+exp(−T^((1−ε)/2)/2))-multiplicatively truthful for any 0<ε<1, improving on Haghtalab et al. (2024).
